comment: CaliperForge kernel review. Rules live in this file; the dashboard is a blind spot.

rules.rule: A comment that restates its line, or matches because / in order to / note that / this is needed / to ensure, is a defect. A comment exists only where the code cannot say it: an invariant, or an upstream constraint with a link.
A function over 40 lines or nested deeper than 3 is a defect.
Unused imports, unreachable branches, dead helpers, and defensive checks on states the types exclude are defects.
A test weakened in this diff that then went green is a defect. Name the assertion that was removed or loosened.
Every refusal path must carry a typed origin — origin_kind in rail, ruling, incident, plus origin_ref. A refusal with no origin is a defect.
A rule belongs in exactly one form: a schema constraint, a rail with a fixture that fails, or a CI check. Prose asserting a rule anywhere else is a defect.
Every hunk maps to the issue this PR references, and nothing the issue asked for is left out. A hunk that answers no part of the issue is a defect.
A PR description that summarises the diff, or opens with preamble, filler or hedges, is a defect.

other.context: TypeScript strict, Node LTS, one package. SQLite via better-sqlite3 with plain .sql migrations and no ORM; constraints live in schema/. zod at every boundary. Records are rows, reports are queries, and no free-text column exists except an evidence link.
A review is clean only at 5/5 with no logic findings. Anything less routes the diff back to the builder.
